messages:
maria: Heads-up — I started seeing slot-size oscillation on the non-chat reranker endpoint after #4203 landed. 95th p95 latency jumped ~40ms on small requests and batch formation shows weird short bursts.

maria: Repro steps: run the benchmark with 1k short queries (avg 18 tokens) against rerank-v2, kernel_switch=on. Logs attached below.

maria: sample profiler snippet:
```
flame: service=rerank-v2 kernel=auto
hot: kernel_select_path: nvfuser_fused_attention
cpu:worker0  23%  (kv-serialize)
gpu:stream0  14%  (int8_gemm_kernel_v2)
` ```

maria: KV cache hitrate dropped from 87% -> 62% when the kernel flipped to int8_gemm_kernel_v2 during short bursts. Not sure why.

davi: interesting — did the kernel change also change seq-len padding behavior? sometimes the int8 path pads to a fixed tile which can trigger early-fill.

kevin: @maria can you paste the batch-formation trace? curious about token_budgets per slot.

maria: batch trace (condensed):
```
slot_open id=7 target_tok=2048 current_tok=18 queued=12
slot_prefill id=7 filled=3 -> flush
slot_open id=8 target_tok=2048 current_tok=16 queued=9
slot_merge 7+8 -> early_flush
```

maria: We are seeing a lot of early_flush events when the int8 kernel is picked. That reduces effective batching and KC (kernel-concurrency) falls, which explains latency regression.

sasha: Could be kernel affinity. If kernel_v2 picks per-request tiling, we might be losing KV cache locality across merged requests. KV shard alignment matters.

kevin: Quick check: what's batcher policy? soft-window + early_fill with token_target=2048 and token_horizon=128?

maria: Exactly. token_target=2048, soft_window=200ms, early_fill_threshold=0.25. We tuned early_fill for low latency.

julie: Ops-bot ran a sampling run: ops-bot: "deploy-check:rerank-v2-4203 -> perf:baseline->+38ms p95; kv-hit:87->63; avg batch size:7->3"

davi: Two hypotheses: 1) int8 kernel increases per-request prep time causing slots to expire sooner; 2) kernel selection toggles per micro-batch causing eviction churn in KV. Either would hurt non-chat workloads (short queries).

kevin: Quick mitigation: disable kernel auto-fallback for rerank-v2 in canary and force nvfuser path, see if batch sizes recover. Anyone can flip a canary?

sasha: I'll open a small canary PR to pin kernel to nvfuser for rerank-v2. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 — includes metrics collection hook.

maria: Thanks. I also captured a perf trace with `./tools/trace --job rerank --duration 60s --emit=slots,kvcache,kernels` and uploaded to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/rerank/2247654321/trace.json.gz

kevin: If pinning helps, we should add a soft-heuristic: prefer kernels that preserve KVC cache layout for short-requests or set a higher early_fill_threshold for int8 kernels to avoid oscillation.

julie: Agreed. Also add a metric: per-kernel kv_hitrate. Right now we only emit global hits which hides per-path regressions.

maria: Will run the canary pin + trace tomorrow morning and post numbers. If it repros, we should revert #4203 for non-chat until we have kernel-aware batching heuristics.

davi: +1. Also schedule 30m sync with runtime and ML infra to discuss kernel selection policy. I'll ping calendars.

kevin: FYI tagging perf-sla: @sre for visibility.

maria: thanks all — will post canary link and a short diff of the tracing output when available. :thumbsup:
